agent_assumptions: Wall representative plane = measured pixel line centrelines/outer faces from pixel_profile scans, not nominal 240mm offsets.

North window sill1.0/head3.4m, South windows sill1.0/head2.8m (directly measured from elevations). East facade openings re-measured directly; large east window head3.4m, two small east windows head2.8m, all sill 1.0m.
West facade opening heights assumed equal to North sill1.0/head3.4m; not independently re-measured (inherited unresolved limitation).
All doors assumed 2.4m height, base 0 (floor level).
Building height 4.5m used uniformly as the single floor's wall height per all four elevations.

CORRECTED THIS RUN: the SE area previously merged as one open room ('CorridorN_SE_open' spanning the whole SE zone) is now split by a newly identified physical divider P7 (stepped wall x400,y753 -> x461,y753 -> x461,y700 -> x611,y700) with its own door (D_SE_divider, x558-592,y700). Direct pixel_profile evidence shows this wall IS connected at both ends (to the corridor wall at x400,y753 and to the exterior east wall at x611,y700), contradicting the inherited draft's unverified claim that it was a non-connecting fragment. The corridor/open-office region (CorridorN_SE_open) now occupies the area north of P7 (including the P6b-bounded pocket x462-610,y585-700 and the small notch x400-461,y700-753, both open to the corridor spine with no wall between them). A new room 'RoomSE_south' occupies the area south of P7 (x400-611,y753-878 plus the sliver x461-611,y700-753), containing a narrow cabinet/desk and 2 chairs, the south-wall door SD1 and window SW2, connected to the corridor pocket via D_SE_divider.
Room roles (reception, office, boardroom, meeting, pantry, corridor/open office) are inferred from furniture symbols, not labelled in the source.
Plan spaces were compiled deterministically from the declared footprint and physical partition segments; no snapping, extension, clipping, or inferred partition was applied.
unresolved: Fine sub-dimension chain sums did not exactly reconcile with outer brackets in earlier drafts on other facades; outer-bracket/pixel-measured boundaries were trusted over the fine labels there. Not re-examined this run.

West facade opening sill/head heights not independently re-measured from elevation pixel dimensions this run; still assumed equal to the North window pattern (sill1.0/head3.4m), inherited unresolved limitation.
RoomSE_south's precise use/role is not labelled in the source; inferred only from furniture symbols (narrow cabinet/desk + 2 chairs).

North/South/West facade opening pixel positions and most interior partitions were preserved unchanged from the prior (unverified) draft per this run's bounded scope; only the SE divider (P7) and its door were newly investigated and corrected this run using direct pixel evidence.
Pixel-to-world calibration was supplied by the caller and was not independently verified.

plan_compilation.basis: Outer wall faces measured via pixel_profile (gray wall fill threshold): west face x=248, east face x=611 (10.0m span); north face y=151, south face y=878 (20.0m span). Internal partitions use measured wall-line pixel centrelines from view_pixel_profile scans. SE divider (P7) re-derived this run: view_pixel_profile axis=x/y scans in box x=390-620,y=555-880 (1f_view.png) show a continuous gray wall band forming a stepped path from the corridor wall (x400) at y753, east to x461, north to y700, then east to the exterior east wall x611, with a door gap x558-592 at y700 (cyan arc+leaf visible in crop [440,685,615,765]). This contradicts the inherited draft's claim of a non-connecting fragment: the path is fully connected at both ends (west end merges into corridor wall x400 at y753; east end merges into exterior wall x611 at y700).

source_geometry_self_consistency.scope: source geometry, contacts and explicit opening hosts

agent_assumptions: Wall representative plane = measured pixel line centrelines/outer faces from pixel_profile scans, not nominal 240mm offsets.

Exterior opening heights this run are re-derived per facade from each elevation's own explicit dimension-chain labels, cross-checked by direct pixel measurement of wall-top/ground datums and the opening graphics themselves, rather than copied across facades.
North entrance door ND1 and South door SD1: z=[0.2,2.6]m, confirmed by strong pixel-to-label match (1900/2400/200 chain) on each facade independently.

East door ED1: z=[0.2,2.6]m assigned by close pixel-graphic match to the same door family as North/South (no separate adjacent explicit label found; the nearby 1100/2400/1000 label was determined to belong to the adjacent EW1 window instead, confirmed by a much closer pixel match to EW1's own graphic). This remains a documented inference, flagged in unresolved.

North window NW1 z=[1.0,3.4]; South windows SW1/SW2 z=[1.0,2.8]; East large window EW1 z=[1.0,3.4] (own 1100/2400/1000 chain, confirmed by close pixel match); East small windows EW2/EW3 z=[1.0,2.8] (EW3 confirmed via its own adjacent 1700/1800/1000 chain; EW2 assumed same small-window family, approximate pixel match).

West small windows WW1-WW4 z=[1.0,2.8]m: CORRECTED this run from the inherited assumption of matching North (1.0/3.4). West_view.png's own left-side chain (1700/1800/1000) is the only dimension evidence for these repeated openings and matches the South-window family instead.
West large boardroom window WW5 z=[1.0,3.4]m: unchanged; confirmed via West_view.png's own right-side chain (1100/2400/1000) adjacent to that specific window.

All interior (non-exterior) doors (D_lobby_corr, D_w2_corr, D_w3_corr, D_w4_corr, D_e2_corr, D_e3_corr, D_SE_divider) retain the prior explicit assumption z=[0,2.4]m: no elevation drawing shows interior partition door heights, so this remains an assumption, not independently re-verified this run (no conflicting evidence found).
